chapter.title: Spotting what changed

cards.body:
The clipping service does not read the whole paper twice. They lay today's page over yesterday's, hold both up to the window, and cut out only the lines that don't line up.

**The scissors cut where the two copies differ, nowhere else.** Every line that matches goes straight in the bin.
cards.simpler: The clipping service does not read the whole paper twice. They put today's page on top of yesterday's and hold both up to the window. Where the two pages match, the light shows one clean line. Where they differ, the lines don't line up. **The scissors cut where the two copies differ, nowhere else.** Every matching line goes straight in the bin. Only the mismatched lines get kept.

cards.prompt: Northwind's pricing page is 400 lines long. Yesterday one line said 'Pro plan: $29 a month'. Today that line says 'Pro plan: $35 a month'. Nothing else moved. What should the clipping hold?

options.text: All 400 lines, so you have the full context.
2 lines: the $29 line marked as gone, the $35 line marked as new.
Just the word 'price', since that is the topic that changed.

whyNot.a: That's the saved copy, not the clipping: the scissors only cut where the two copies differ, and 398 lines matched.
whyNot.c: That's a summary, not a comparison: the clipping keeps the actual lines, word for word, so you can quote them later.

cards.reteach: Picture both pages held up to the light. 398 lines sit perfectly on top of each other and vanish. Only the 2 price lines stick out, and those are what you keep.

cards.title: Lines in, lines out
cards.body:
A *diff* is a line-by-line comparison of 2 text files. It walks down both at once and sorts every line into 3 piles: in both, only in yesterday's, only in today's.

The 'in both' pile is thrown away. Lines only in yesterday's copy are printed with a minus sign: gone. Lines only in today's copy get a plus sign: new. **A changed line shows up as one minus and one plus**, because to the diff it is an old line that left and a new line that arrived.

You don't write this yourself. Your Mac has a command called diff built in, and most languages ship one too.
cards.simpler: A *diff* is a tool that compares 2 text files line by line, like checking two shopping lists side by side. It sorts every line into 3 piles: in both, only in yesterday's, only in today's. The 'in both' pile is thrown away. Lines only in yesterday's get a minus sign: gone. Lines only in today's get a plus sign: new. **A changed line shows up as one minus and one plus**, an old line leaving and a new one arriving. You don't write this yourself. Your Mac has a command called diff built in.

cards.title: The page that changed every day
cards.body:
Priya set up diffs on a rival's changelog page and got a hit on day 1. Exciting. The output was 2 lines: minus 'Last updated: 3 March', plus 'Last updated: 4 March'.

Day 2, same thing with the next date. Day 3, same. The page was 'changing' every morning and saying nothing new. The diff was doing its job perfectly. It just had no idea that a date stamp isn't news.
cards.simpler: Priya set up a diff on a rival's changelog page. On day 1 she got a hit. The output was 2 lines: minus 'Last updated: 3 March', plus 'Last updated: 4 March'. Day 2, same thing with the next date. Day 3, same again. The page was 'changing' every morning but saying nothing new. The diff was doing its job perfectly. It just had no idea that a date stamp isn't news.

cards.prompt: You run a diff on 2 copies of a rival's pricing page. The output is exactly this: minus 'Starter: up to 5 users', plus 'Starter: up to 10 users'. What happened?

options.text: The Starter plan was removed from the page.
The Starter line changed: it now says 10 users instead of 5.
A second Starter plan was added alongside the first.

whyNot.a: That's a removal only, which would be a minus line with no matching plus: here a plus line arrived in its place.
whyNot.c: That's an addition only, which would be a plus with no minus: the minus line shows the old version left.

cards.reteach: A diff can't say 'edited'. It only knows 'left' and 'arrived'. So one edited line always appears as a pair: the old text with a minus, the new text with a plus. Read the pair together.

cards.title: The scissors are not clever
cards.body:
A diff compares characters, not meaning. **It flags anything that differs, including noise**: today's date, 'posted 3 minutes ago', a rotating banner, logos in a random order. Priya's fix was to drop any line containing 'Last updated' before comparing. You will build a short ignore list like this for each page, and that is normal.

An empty diff is not a failure. It means both copies exist and match, so there is nothing to report today. A missing copy is a different problem, and you add a check for it in chapter 7.

Always compare today's copy with yesterday's, not with the first one you ever saved.
cards.simpler: A diff compares letters, not meaning. **It flags anything that differs, including noise**: today's date, 'posted 3 minutes ago', a rotating banner, logos in a random order. Priya's fix was to drop any line with 'Last updated' before comparing. You will build a short ignore list like this for each page. That is normal. An empty diff is not a failure. It means both copies exist and match, so nothing to report today. A missing copy is a different problem, covered in chapter 7. Always compare today's copy with yesterday's, not the first one you saved.

cards.body:
Tom saved his first copy on a Monday and, every day after, compared today's page with that Monday file. By Friday his diff was 60 lines long and the same price change from Tuesday was in it for the fourth time.

Spot it: **if the same change keeps showing up day after day**, you are comparing against the wrong day. Each morning, yesterday's file is the one to hold up to the light.
cards.simpler: Tom saved his first copy on a Monday. Every day after, he compared today's page with that same Monday file. By Friday his diff was 60 lines long. The same price change from Tuesday was in it for the fourth time. Spot it: **if the same change keeps showing up day after day**, you are comparing against the wrong day. Each morning, yesterday's file is the one to hold up to the light, not the first one.

cards.prompt: Wednesday morning the agent fetches a rival's blog page. Tuesday's and Wednesday's copies are both saved, and the diff comes back with 0 lines. What does that tell you?

options.text: The fetch failed, so there was nothing to compare.
The page is identical to yesterday's. Nothing changed, nothing to report.
The diff needs the whole page sent to the model to decide.

whyNot.a: That's a missing copy, not an empty diff: here both files exist, so the comparison ran and found a perfect match.
whyNot.c: That's the model's job in chapter 5, not the diff's: the diff has already decided, and its answer is 'no difference'.

cards.reteach: Two copies held up to the light, and every line sits on top of its twin. Nothing sticks out, so the scissors never cut. Zero lines is a real answer: no news today.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: A diff lays today's copy over yesterday's and **keeps only the lines that are new or gone**, with an edited line showing as one gone plus one new. It flags noise like dates too, so you trim those out, and an empty diff just means a quiet day.
cards.simpler: A diff lays today's copy over yesterday's and **keeps only the lines that are new or gone**. An edited line shows up as one line gone plus one line new. The diff also flags noise like dates, so you trim those out before comparing. An empty diff is not a problem. It just means a quiet day with nothing changed on the page.

cards.body: Open Terminal. Copy your chapter 3 file, change one line in the copy, then run diff on the two files. Read the minus and plus lines out loud. Under a minute.
cards.simpler: Open Terminal, the app on your Mac that takes typed commands. Copy your chapter 3 file. Change one line in the copy. Then run diff on the two files, the old one and the new one. Read the minus line and the plus line out loud. The minus is the old line that left. The plus is the new line that arrived. This takes under a minute.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now run a comparison between 2 saved copies of a page and point to exactly which lines were added or removed.
